Definition: from G1680; to expect or confide:--(have, thing) hope(-d) (for), trust.
BiblicalUsage: The word elpízō carries the sense of to hope, to trust. In Matthew 12:21, the text says "And in his name shall the Gentiles trust." In Luke 6:34, the text says "And if ye lend [to them] of whom ye hope to receive."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading elpízō this way, I believe hope is not wishing; it is trusting God for what He has promised, even before we see it. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
